RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 40

An all-male panel may reflect systemic representation issues or unconscious affinity bias, but it is not definitive proof of discrimination. The selected candidate holds relevant qualifications, and civil service decisions generally rely on interview scoring rubrics.

Whether to raise it depends on your jurisdiction’s rules. Many public sector policies explicitly require gender-balanced panels. If formal guidelines were breached, you have clear procedural grounds to query the process. 

First, chase your written feedback to examine how candidates were evaluated against the core competencies. If you later raise the panel's composition, frame it as an inquiry regarding compliance with recruitment diversity protocols rather than leading with an accusation.
